educationalGoal: In Japanese Communication 3, students aim for further development of basic grammar through communication tasks. Students will focus on developing skills of communic ation in modern Japanese reading, writing, speaking, and listening.
advice: Students will learn to conduct daily conversations in Japanese and deal with basic daily situations by focusing on fluency of basic grammar. Social and cultural manners and gestures necessary for appropriate communication wi th native speakers will also be introduced and reinforced with practical communication activities. This course has a Moodle course site. All important information about course related matters will be posted on t his site. It is students' responsibility to check the site regularly.

requiredKnowledge: Students must have completed Genki I grammar or possess equivalent knowledge or Japanese 100 level with a grade of C or higher.

小テスト ① レ Daily review quizzes will assess students' understanding of grammar structures, kanji, vocabul ary, and culturally appropriate usage. Quizzes are usually given at the beginning of class.   ② レ   ③ レ   ④ レ   ⑤ レ   ⑥     レポート ① レ Students will take turns presenting a kanji they have found in real-life contexts, such as sig ns, menus, or instructions. This activity helps build practical kanji knowledge and encourages students to engage with the language in their daily environment. Kanji introduced may be incl uded in review quizzes.   ② レ   ③ レ   ④ レ   ⑤ レ   ⑥     成果発表
(口頭・実技) ① レ Students will give a short in-class speech (approximately 1 minute). The speech should be base d on a personal experience, such as a recent event, cultural observation, travel experience, o r daily life in Japan. This activity is designed to improve spoken fluency, build confidence, and encourage cultural exchange. Students are expected to prepare in advance and speak without reading a full script.   ② レ   ③ レ   ④ レ   ⑤ レ   ⑥     作品 ①      ②     ③     ④     ⑤     ⑥     ポートフォリオ ① レ Students are required to complete a project of their own choosing. They must make three report s to the instructor. The first report will be the project proposal, and students must have the instructor’s permission to start. The mid-term report must be submitted. The final report (c ompleted project) must be submitted at the end of the course. Students will also be required t o give a presentation of their completed project.   ② レ   ③
